transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says the Trump administration has warned it could
cut off intelligence sharing unless the country stops drone strikes on Russian oil refineries.
NPR's Joanna Kekissis spoke to Zelensky.
Zelensky told NPR that the Trump administration's decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel
will not bring down fuel prices.
He says the Iran war has blocked fuel transport through the Strait of Hormuz.
"Mostly people in the world know why their prices on any kind of energy, including diesel,
raised up, why they increased.
Because of blocking the Strait of Hormuz, everybody understands it."
President Trump blames Ukraine for rising diesel prices.
He has demanded Ukraine stop its deep strikes on Russian energy sites.
Zelensky says Ukraine wants to weaken the Kremlin's ability to wage war.
He says Ukraine will not stop these strikes unless Russia also stops attacking Ukraine's
energy grid.
Joanna Kekissis, NPR News, KU.
A judge has sentenced the man convicted for the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur.
Steve Futterman reports.
"The judge ruled Dwayne Davis should be sentenced to 40 years to life.
Under Nevada law, he will have to serve a minimum of 40 years.
And at age 63, it's very unlikely Davis will ever leave prison alive."
Before the sentence was announced, the court heard statements from Tupac Shakur's sister
and brother.
They both talked about the loss they feel, and they also talked about the world missing
the potential of Tupac Shakur as he developed as an artist.
Throughout the hearing, Dwayne Davis stood, and when the judge announced her sentence,
he showed virtually no emotion.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman at the County Courthouse in Las Vegas.
The window is closing today to register to vote for the midterm elections in some states,
NPR's Hansi Lo Wong reports.
There are only hours left for eligible voters to register or update their registration in
time for the midterms in Kansas, Louisiana, New Jersey, Oregon and West Virginia.
And there's less than a week left until the next major voter registration deadline on
Monday, October 19.
That's in three states, Alabama, Pennsylvania and South Dakota, as well as Guam.
If you're already registered, election officials recommend confirming your status and updating
your contact information before the deadline.
Voters can be removed from lists, especially if they've recently moved, changed their
name or haven't voted in a while.
You can check your voter registration status by visiting your state or territory's official
election website.
Hansi Lo Wong, NPR News.
President Trump's ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, has resigned after allegations
that she asked a Republican donor to pay off her 100,000 American Express Card bill.
She says she'll vigorously defend herself earlier.
President Trump was asked if he was considering firing Guilfoyle and said he was looking at
it and was not happy.
In the face of shrinking health budgets, the World Health Organization is updating guidance
to make limited vaccine stocks cover more people, NPR's Jonathan Lambert reports.
Many global vaccination campaigns are funded through foreign aid.
As the U.S. and many other countries drastically reduce such spending, many countries are facing
tighter vaccine budgets.
On Tuesday, the WHO's Vaccine Advisory Committee recommended smaller dosing regimens for several
vaccines.
They recommended that yellow fever vaccine campaigns use 1/5 the typical dose for a single
vaccine when there are supply or budgetary constraints to help get the shots into more
arms.
And the committee said that the HPV vaccine campaign should use a single dose instead
of a two- or three-dose schedule.
The committee stressed that evidence suggests these smaller regimens are still effective
and could ultimately help more people get vaccinated.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
Formula One says Rwanda will host a race in the early 2030s when the series returns to
Africa for the first time in almost 40 years.
Drivers say the track will be built near an under-construction airport serving the capital
and will use hills and dips in the landscape to challenge drivers.
The last time F1 raced in Africa was the South African Grand Prix in 1993.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
This message comes from IXL, a learning platform for helping kids build confidence and get
up to speed fast.

topics.text: Zelensky says Trump administration threatened intelligence cutoff over Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries
Dwayne Davis sentenced to 40 years to life for the 1996 killing of Tupac Shakur in Las Vegas
Voter registration deadlines approach for midterms in Kansas, Louisiana, New Jersey, Oregon, West Virginia
Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle resigns amid allegations she asked donor to pay her Amex bill
WHO updates vaccine guidance recommending smaller doses to stretch limited stocks amid aid cuts
Formula One to hold a race in Rwanda in the early 2030s, marking return to Africa
